Platform & Automation Policy

How PULL GTM connects to third-party platforms, uses AI to support go-to-market work, and sets boundaries for responsible research, messaging, and automated actions.

Effective: 18 October 2026  ·  Applies to: PULL GTM users and connected workflows

01. Scope and purpose

PULL GTM (“PULL”) is a software service for business research, opportunity qualification, workflow preparation and, where enabled, authorized actions using connected third-party services. This policy describes the conditions for using PULL's automation and integrations responsibly.

Not every integration or automation described here is available in the current release. Functionality is enabled only when supported by PULL, the connected provider, the permissions granted, and applicable law. A planned capability is not a promise of availability.

This document is a platform-use policy. It is not a substitute for a complete Privacy Notice, Terms of Service, Data Processing Agreement, or jurisdiction-specific legal advice.

02. Authorized account and platform access

Users may connect only accounts, workspaces, stores, pages or communication channels that they own or are authorized to administer. PULL must use official provider authentication and APIs where required, request permissions appropriate to the action, and respect provider access conditions.

Signing into PULL does not grant PULL permission to read a Gmail mailbox, send WhatsApp messages, access an Instagram inbox, or operate any other external account. Each external connection requires its own authorization.

  • Do not submit someone else's credentials, reuse stolen access tokens, or bypass authentication, access limits or platform controls.
  • Do not use unauthorized scraping, browser bots, account impersonation, bulk account creation or deceptive automation.
  • Users must be able to review applicable access, and connected authorizations should be revocable through PULL and, where necessary, the provider.
  • A “connected” status should be based on verified authorization, not merely an API key being saved or an integration being listed.

03. Messaging, outreach, and consent

Users are responsible for ensuring every communication has an appropriate lawful basis and follows the recipient's preferences, local marketing laws, and the destination platform's rules. A publicly visible profile or phone number does not automatically grant permission to send automated marketing messages.

PULL may support preparing drafts, requesting approval, handling eligible inbound inquiries, or executing permitted outbound actions. A prepared draft is not a sent message. Any automated send must satisfy the applicable account permissions, consent or other lawful basis, content restrictions, and workflow authorization.

  • Respect opt-outs, unsubscribe requests, blocked contacts and do-not-contact records across relevant workflows.
  • Do not send unsolicited bulk messages, misleading claims, harassment, fake engagement, or repeated messages designed to evade limits.
  • Do not disguise an automated response as a human interaction when disclosure is required by law or platform rules.
  • Marketing campaigns must use the relevant sender identification and unsubscribe or opt-out mechanisms where required.
  • Follow any message-template, conversation-window, recipient-initiated conversation and rate-limit rules set by the provider.

04. Platform-specific boundaries

External platforms provide different capabilities and can revise them without notice. The table below describes important restrictions, not a representation that each connection is currently active.

ChannelRequired boundaries
LinkedInPersonal messaging, scraping and browser-driven automation are restricted. Use only expressly authorized APIs and permissions; otherwise use reviewed, manual handoff.
WhatsApp BusinessUse an eligible business account, valid messaging permission and approved templates or conversation windows where required.
Instagram / FacebookMessaging and publishing depend on eligible accounts, asset access, approved Meta permissions and eligible conversations.
XAPI entitlement, recipient intent, automation restrictions and anti-spam rules govern posts, replies and direct messages.
Gmail / emailSender authorization, suitable API scopes, applicable email-marketing laws, suppression and deliverability requirements apply.
Shopify / marketplacesOnly authorized merchant data and permitted platform interfaces may be used; marketplace listings do not grant access to buyer identities or private search activity.

PULL is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or certified by these providers merely because it offers a compatible integration. Each provider's current terms take precedence over a conflicting automation instruction.

05. AI outputs, prospect discovery, and evidence

AI-generated recommendations, drafts, matching scores and research summaries may be incomplete or inaccurate. PULL must distinguish verified facts, user-provided information, public signals, inferences and unknowns. Users must review material claims before taking consequential action.

PULL does not claim access to the identity of individual people making private Google searches, hidden buyer databases, private financial records, or restricted platform data without a lawful and authorized source. A signal of interest is not proof of purchasing power, intent to buy, or consent to contact.

Neither a requested number of leads nor an AI confidence score guarantees a corresponding number of verified people, sales or conversions.

06. Personal data and user responsibilities

Use only data you are entitled to collect, import, share and process for the specified business purpose. Apply data minimization, appropriate transparency, accuracy checks, access controls and reasonable retention practices. Do not upload sensitive information unless the feature explicitly supports it and a lawful basis exists.

PULL must preserve account separation and use permission-limited access for connected providers. Users remain responsible for the legitimacy of their source records, notices, campaign audiences and consent evidence. Exported data must be protected by the recipient.

Privacy obligations may include the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 and, where applicable, other regional privacy and electronic-marketing rules. Data rights and privacy requests may be submitted using the contact below, subject to identity verification and applicable law.

Additional details about actual data categories, service providers, retention periods, transfers, deletion procedures and legal bases belong in a separately maintained Privacy Notice.

07. Automation controls and auditability

Where an execution capability is available, PULL should enforce permissions before any external action, preserve approval requirements, validate current eligibility and suppression records, and prevent duplicate or uncontrolled retries. Users must not attempt to evade these controls.

Actions have distinct states: prepared, approved, submitted, delivered (only when supported by provider evidence), failed or uncertain. A provider accepting a submission is not proof that a person received, read or replied to it.

Some workflows may be automatic within the scope explicitly authorized by the account owner. Other actions require fresh review or direct human handoff. PULL may pause an action when authorization, consent, source quality, provider access or system status cannot be established.

08. Feature availability, charges, and reliability

Features vary by plan, region, connected account, developer-app approval, API availability and rollout status. Third-party providers may impose rate limits, usage charges, messaging fees, verification requirements, restrictions or interruptions.

No integration provides a guarantee of uninterrupted service, unrestricted automation, message delivery, prospect accuracy or sales results. A third-party fee is not included in PULL unless expressly stated in applicable product pricing.

09. Licences, assurance, and certification claims

PULL's status as a software application does not by itself establish that it is licensed as an Internet Service Provider (ISP). Internet-access and other regulated communications services may require separate licences depending on the actual service offered and jurisdiction.

Adopting security or privacy practices does not equal third-party certification. No ISO/IEC 27001 certificate, SOC 2 report, regulatory approval, or platform-partner designation is represented by this policy. Such claims must be supported by genuine, current evidence and an identified issuing or assessing body before being displayed.

Users should not present PULL-generated material as independently certified, legally cleared or officially endorsed by an external platform unless supported by verifiable documentation.

10. Misuse, enforcement, and policy updates

PULL may restrict, pause or disable access to a workflow or connection when needed to protect users, recipients, the service, or provider compliance. Serious or repeated violations may lead to account restrictions subject to applicable agreements and law.

We may update this policy as our capabilities, applicable laws or third-party rules change. The effective date at the top identifies this version. Material changes should be communicated through appropriate product notices where required.
